content.development: One continuous world, composed from catalogued rules (no blueprint fits a mechanism demo framed by two scope-widening pull-backs). The request rate limiter's identity opens like a lid to reveal what runs underneath: one full bucket. Camera move 1 pulls back to show that this bucket sits in the front slot of a central host, with other users' buckets in rows behind it. The camera then holds while one user's numbered requests play out a fixed token ledger. First comes a balanced exchange: one request takes a token, then one drip puts it back. Next a burst takes six tokens while the steady drip ring adds only one, so the bucket runs dry. The next request arrives at the empty bucket and is turned away, and the drip carries on refilling at its own pace. Camera move 2 pulls back again to name the host as Redis, with its two ways to run it. Every count on screen follows one ledger, so the viewer can check why the eighth request fails: five starting tokens plus two drips can admit at most seven.

demonstration.text: Illustrative ledger, in this exact event order (T = tokens in the bucket): start full, T=5 → request #1 takes a token and passes, T=4 → drip D1, T=5 → burst: #2 T=4, #3 T=3, #4 T=2, #5 T=1 → drip D2, T=2 → #6 T=1 → #7 T=0, the bucket is dry → #8 arrives at the empty bucket and is rejected, T=0 → drip D3, T=1 → drip D4 lands during the Redis pull-back, T=2. Admissions: 5 starting tokens + 2 drips (D1, D2) before the rejection = 7 admitted (#1–#7); the 8th is the first refused. The drip interval is fixed, and six requests (#2–#7) arrive within a single drip interval. Rule for construction: whatever the final audio timing, #8 must arrive after #7 empties the bucket and before D3 lands, and no drip may fall between #7 and #8.
